caption: The drawing shows a single lidded urn or vessel rendered in pencil on a beige background. The urn, positioned centrally within a large rectangular frame, has a rounded, bulbous body that tapers down to a narrow stem and sits on a wide, circular base. The lid is domed with a small, outward-flaring handle or knop on top and a prominent rim that extends outwards. Shading is used to create the illusion of depth and curvature, giving the object a three-dimensional appearance. Below and to the left of the main urn, there is a smaller, simplified line drawing of the same vessel enclosed in a square frame, showing only the outlines without shading or detail. The drawing uses only grayscale tones throughout, with no additional colors or patterns.
title: Silver Sugar Bowl
cluster: #19 — Ceramic Arts: Pottery, Stoneware, and Porcelain
